To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

prolonged activation of the transcription factors STAT1, 3, and 5 results from association of their respective cytokine receptors with the EGF receptor, which in tumour cells is constitutively active.

prolonged activation of the transcription factors STAT3 and STAT1 results from association of gp130 with epidermal growth receptor (EGFR), leading to EGFR activation of STAT3 and STAT3-dependent transcription, and that this prolonged activation is not inhibited by suppressor of cytokines 3 (SOX3).

the IL-6–induced STAT3 signaling response to invading pathogens can be prolonged in the absence of further exposure to IL-6 by the binding of gp130 to the EGFR, which rephosphorylates STAT3 and is not inhibited by binding of SOCS3 to gp130 and to JAKs 2 and 1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the transcription factor signal transducers and activators of transcription 3 (STAT3).
understanding how the immune system is activated to respond to pathogens and how the inflammatory response is turned off.

the regulation of signal transduction by the transcription factor STAT 3 in response to cytokines of the IL 6 family, and in particular, the mechanisms that control the magnitude, duration and specificity of STAT 3 activation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
STAT3 activation in response IL-6 is extended by binding of the IL- 6 receptor to the EGFR.
STAT3 activation in response IL-6 is sustained by the binding of gp130 to EGFR.

the activation of STAT3 in response IL-6 is normally terminated by SOCS3 but that in some circumstances the IL-6R can bind to the EGFR, leading, via EGFR, to reactivation of STAT3, and this second wave of STAT is not terminated by SOCS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

IL-6 and EGFR are both required for normal development, and that in the presence of IL-6, the EGFR is able to prolong STAT3 activation, which in turn supports sustained expression of some of the proteins that play important and often opposing roles in inflammation and tumorigenesis.
IL-6-induced STAT3 activation is terminated by SOCS3 binding, which prevents further STAT3 phosphorylation, and is prolonged by EGFR activation, which rephosphorylates STAT3.

prolonged activation of the transcriptional regulator STAT3 results from the association of the IL6 receptor with the EGFR, which in turn rephosphorylates STAT3 in a manner not blocked by SOCS3, and that this prolonged activation supports sustained expression by a subset of proteins important in inflammation and cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EGFR is a key regulator of STAT3 signaling.
STAT3 activation in response IL-6 can be prolonged by the binding to the IL-6R of the EGF receptor, which activates STAT3 in the presence of SOCS-3.

the activation of STAT3 is prolonged by the interaction of the IL-5 receptor with EGFR, and this prolonged activation supports the sustained expression of a set of genes that play important roles both in cancer and in inflammation.
